EDAG Engineering Scandinavia AB is a Gothenburg-based company with a familiar atmosphere and at the same time the potential of a global world-class development company. With our 120 consultants we are the largest independent German consultant company in the region. Within the group we are over 8500 employees all over the world and direct supplier to major automotive companies and their suppliers, which is our core business.
EDAG is characterized by a familiar atmosphere where everyone has the opportunity to be seen. We are proud of our good team spirit, which we build through joint activities such as everything from education to wellness.

Description
HIL developer & test engineer.
EDAG is developing HIL rigs together with customer and we need persons that can operate it and support our customer onsite in how to use it for testing. The person are expected to participate in develop test cases and verification methods and to perform functional testing of the power conversion and charging system and its components.
Knowledge in these tools and environments is important:
Vector CANoe
Matlab/Simulink
Python
GIT

We need test engineer that can start in October (or within a month) and the assignment is 6-12 months depending on customer requirements.
Our requirements
Master or Bachelor of Science in Engineering within Mechatronics, Electronics, Data Science or similar.
Ability to communicate in an easy and understandable way
Experience from Agile development is meritorious
Good communication skills in English and Swedish, both spoken and written is required.

We offer
We welcome you in to our open and diverse culture. We promise you a lot of opportunities to grow and learn as you become a part of a dynamic and creative team who are at the top of their field. With leading-edge technology, we help our customer’s vision become a reality. We are an engineer’s playground of innovation and creativity that is fast, furious and fun!
If you are ready to be a part of the team that brings Tomorrow here Today, send in your application to career@edag.se, marked “HIL Developer & Test 2021015"

Job Scope 
Why does the role exist? High level purpose of function. 

This role is a part of Quality Control team responsible for establishing a cell validation function to develop and execute validation plan, to identify optimized Test & Validation methodologies, enabling for a digitalized production Test & Validation function. Ensuring the sustainable scaling of the function through standardization, best practice adoption from Test & Validation Västerås and develop learning from partner testing institutes.  

This role may require occasional international / domestic travel.

Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to)  

Play a key role within the Quality Technology team to fully digitalize cell validation.  

Analyse and share test results to internal stakeholders and customers.   

Collaborate with Västerås departments and engineering to develop Test & Validation strategies which deliver both optimization and enable production scaling.  

Plan, organize, direct and follow up on project-related testing activities.   

Contribute to the creation and implementation of policies, guidelines, and procedures to aid and improve business and operational performance, including HSE.  

Continuously innovating and developing the Test & Validation production hub.  

The main interface to the project and launch teams, responsible for capacity planning, reporting and escalations.    
Work closely with the central and local Test & Validation teams to plan and optimize workflow, whilst meeting contractual obligations to the customers.   

Support in driving the digitalization of the T&V operating model, including data driven scheduling, KPI reporting and results traceability.   

Support projects including establishing new testing facilities, managing and documenting test specifications, and coordinating cross functionally to ensure successful execution.   

Requirements 

Educational background and previous experience required for the role. 

Qualifications and experience  

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant subject.  

5+ years of experience working in a high throughput manufacturing environment.  

2+ years of experience as a Project Manager, Product Engineer, or similar.  

 Specific skills and Knowledge 

Expert user of SharePoint, Excel, and PowerPoint.  

Proficiency with SQL and data visualization tools (Power BI, Looker, Tableau, etc.) preferred but not required.  

Effective communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts to a non-technical audience.  
Ability to identify business objectives and set clear, measurable goals for the team to achieve the vision.  

Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams.

3+ years of experience in a metrology or quality engineering role, preferably in the battery, automotive, or electronics industry. 
Minimum a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Metrology, or related field. 
Hands-on experience with metrology equipment. 
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification is preferred.

Proficiency in metrology software such as Fluke MET/CAL, Beamex, Druck 4Sight2, or similar.

Quick facts
🧑‍🍳 Role: Dishwasher, hourly, on-demand assignments

💰 Pay: 153 - 165 kr/h

🕝 Hours: Daytime, evenings, weekends — you set your own availability

📍 Where: Göteborg — restaurants, hotels and kitchens across the city

The job
You keep the kitchen running. Dish and glass wash, pot wash, and a clean back of house. High tempo during service, reset in between. Some shifts you're alone in the dish pit, some shifts you're two or three. Since you work across different kitchens, the exact setup changes — you get the details before each assignment.
You need
At least 1 year of experience from a professional kitchen

To show up on time and hold a steady pace

To handle a physical job — standing, lifting, heat, humidity

Basic Swedish or English

Basic hygiene awareness

How it works
Work at different places — sometimes several in one week, sometimes longer assignments

You get job offers in good time and decide how much and when you work

153 - 165 kr/h

Flexible pay through Cappy: see what you've worked and earned, and withdraw your pay between paydays — possible within 24h after a shift

A personal staffing company built for hotels and restaurants, with offices in Gothenburg, Malmö and Stockholm. Several hundred employees. Our clients range from neighbourhood restaurants to hotel chains — and we pick them carefully, so you end up in kitchens worth working in.
How to apply
Answer the questions in the next step, attach your CV (no cover letter needed) and leave your contact details.
Process: phone interview → first assignment. Your first shift is a real, paid job — that's how we get to know each other. If your experience checks out, we move fast: you can be out working within days.

Founding Software Engineer 
Finna is building a personal cloud computer (Matrix) for the AI-agent era: a persistent environment where people can run coding agents, tools, applications, and long-running work without tying everything to one laptop.
We believe AI agents need more than chat windows. They need durable computers with memory, software, files, permissions, terminals, and continuity across devices.
We are looking for a Founding Software Engineer to join Finna AB in a full-time role based in Stockholm, with flexibility to work remotely within Sweden.
What you will do
You will work directly with the founding team across software engineering, product engineering, technical architecture, implementation, debugging, testing, deployment, and related technical support.
Your responsibilities will include:
Develop and maintain software across backend systems, infrastructure, and user-facing product surfaces.
Own technical work from architecture and implementation through testing, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
Build reliable systems for persistent AI-agent sessions, cloud computers, terminals, files, applications, and realtime communication.
Work with TypeScript services, Linux environments, PostgreSQL, APIs, realtime protocols, and modern web technologies.
Investigate and resolve technical and operational problems.
Improve system security, reliability, performance, observability, and maintainability.
Work closely with users and the founding team to turn product needs into durable technical solutions.
Contribute to technical direction, engineering practices, and product decisions.

What we are looking for
Demonstrated experience building and shipping substantial software products or systems.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, including APIs, data modelling, testing, debugging, and system design.
Strong TypeScript skills and comfort working with Linux and PostgreSQL.
Ability to work across backend infrastructure and user-facing product code.
Good judgment around security, reliability, permissions, and data protection.
High ownership and the ability to take work from an initial problem through production.
Clear written and spoken English.
Ability to work with substantial overlap with European working hours.

Experience with AI-agent runtimes, cloud infrastructure, terminals, realtime systems, developer tools, React, Electron, or mobile applications is helpful but not required.
We care about ability, judgment, ownership, and evidence of what you have built. We do not require a particular degree, pedigree, previous title, or arbitrary number of years of experience.

About the position
TUSA Energi AB is currently seeking an experienced and results-driven Mechanic Manager to oversee and take full responsibility for mechanical systems, equipment, and on-site installation and maintenance operations in Boden. In this key role, you will ensure that mechanical installations, heavy machinery operations, piping, and mechanical assemblies are executed on schedule, within budget, and in full compliance with the highest safety and quality standards. You will work closely with field personnel, subcontractors, and engineering teams within an international project environment.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and supervise all mechanical assembly, installation, maintenance, and commissioning activities on the construction site.
Manage and ensure the efficient use, regular maintenance, and safety compliance of mechanical equipment, heavy vehicles, and machinery.
Plan, coordinate, and direct the daily work of mechanical subcontractors, technicians, and fitters.
Ensure all mechanical work complies with project schedules, technical specifications, and Swedish safety standards.
Resolve technical deviations and mechanical issues at the interface between design and on-site execution.
Oversee quality control processes, inspection checklists, and mechanical sign-offs.
Strictly enforce Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) regulations within the mechanical scope.

Qualifications
Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent technical background.
Deep technical knowledge of industrial mechanical installations, heavy equipment, piping systems, or HVAC.
Solid understanding of Swedish safety standards, regulations, and industry specifications is considered a strong advantage.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both Swedish and English.
Turkish language skills are considered a significant asset.

Personal Attributes
Strong on-site leadership with a proven ability to motivate and manage teams.
Practical and solution-oriented mindset with the ability to resolve technical field issues swiftly.
High commitment to safety (HSE) and precision in execution.
Decisive and calm under high-pressure conditions and in demanding environments.
Strong collaborative skills within multicultural and international teams.

Employment Conditions & Benefits
Full-time position, 40 hours per week.
Market-based salary based on experience.
Pension and insurance according to Swedish collective standards.
Opportunity to work in a growing international organization on one of Sweden's largest industrial energy projects.
Support for professional development and career progression.

Work Location
Boden, Sweden
Application
Please send your CV and cover letter to:
info@tusaenergi.se

jobs.occupation: Talent Sourcer for a Leading Fashion Company
jobs.description:
Do you want to help identify and attract creative talent for one of Sweden’s most well-known fashion companies? We are currently looking for a Talent Sourcer, apply today!
About the role
Our client is an international Swedish fashion company headquartered in central Stockholm. As a Talent Sourcer, you will work closely with the recruitment team and support the early stages of the recruitment process, focusing on building candidate pipelines, scheduling interviews, and ensuring a high pace of delivery.
You will primarily support high-volume recruitment within creative functions, such as design and product-related roles, where multiple positions need to be filled within a short timeframe. You will join a driven and collaborative team that values knowledge sharing, teamwork, and a positive work environment.
Work tasks
In this role, you will:
Identify and engage relevant candidates through proactive sourcing activities.
Conduct initial screening interviews.
Coordinate and schedule interviews with hiring managers and recruiters.
Ensure candidate information and recruitment processes are accurately maintained within the recruitment system.
Contribute to building strong talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs.

For the right candidate, there will be opportunities to take on greater ownership of the recruitment process.
We are looking for
Has previous experience in sourcing and recruitment.
Experience recruiting for creative roles is considered an advantage.
Is structured, self-driven, and comfortable working towards clear targets.
Has excellent communication skills and thrives in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
Is fluent in both Swedish and English, spoken and written.

As a person, you enjoy working in a goal-oriented recruitment environment where you can drive processes forward, identify the right talent, and create results. You are service-minded, quality-focused, flexible, and adaptable.
Our recruitment process
This recruitment process is handled by Academic Work and it is our client’s wish that all questions regarding the position is directed to Academic Work.
Our selection process is continuous and the advert may close before the recruitment process is completed if we have moved forward to the next phase. The process includes two tests: one personality test and one cognitive test. The tests are tools to find the right talent for the right position, to enable equality, diversity, and a fair process.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Plant Stress and Nitrogen Metabolism
jobs.description:
Department of Forest Ecology and Management
 
Scientific background
Plants do more with organic nitrogen than use it for growth. Amino acids and their derivatives can also be diverted into signalling pathways that shape development and help plants respond to environmental stress. We are seeking a motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to investigate how this redirection of organic nitrogen metabolism is regulated and what it means for plant stress tolerance.
About the position  
The project explores the links between organic nitrogen metabolism, metabolic regulation and downstream signalling cascades, and their roles in plant responses to abiotic and biotic challenges, including pathogen attack. The work will combine physiological, biochemical, molecular and advanced imaging approaches, using Arabidopsis thaliana alongside crop species in sterile, hydroponic and soil-based systems. The position is particularly suitable for a candidate who wishes to build an independent research profile at the interface of plant nutrition, metabolic signalling and stress biology
Key responsibilities
The successful candidate will:
Plan and carry out experiments on plant growth, development and stress responses under controlled conditions
Use chemical and genetic approaches to manipulate organic nitrogen metabolism and signalling
Perform gene expression, metabolite and biochemical analyses
Carry out microscopy-based analyses, including confocal and two-photon imaging
Develop and run stress and infection mimicking bioassays as well as nematode assays
Analyse and interpret data, and publish results in international scientific journals
Contribute to experimental planning and take an active part in the group’s national and international collaborations, and in the supervision of students

Your profile
Required qualifications
PhD in plant biology, plant physiology, molecular biology, biochemistry or a closely related discipline. 
Documented experience with experimental plant research, experimental design and data analysis
Documented scientific publishing in international peer-reviewed journals
Ability to plan, execute and document experiments independently
Very good written and spoken English

Meritorious qualifications
 
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered a strong advantage:
Gene expression analysis, particularly qRT-PCR
In vitro sterile culture techniques
Work with Arabidopsis thaliana and crop species
Two-photon microscopy and advanced confocal microscopy
Hydroponic cultivation and soil-based treatments
Mass spectrometry (MS) and metabolite analysis
Phytopathology and plant–pathogen interactions
Bioassay development and implementation, particularly nematode culture and infection assays

Great importance will be placed on personal qualities such as curiosity, independence, problem-solving ability and the ability to work well with others.
As postdoctoral appointments are career-developing positions for junior researchers, we are primarily looking for candidates with a doctoral degree that is three years old at most. If there are special circumstances, such a degree may have been awarded earlier. Special circumstances include leave due to illness, parental leave, positions of trust within trade union organizations, service within the total defence system, or other similar circumstances, as well as clinical service or other employment/assignments relevant to the subject area.
 
About us  
The position is based at the Department of Forest Ecology and Management at SLU in Umeå, within the research group led by Professor Torgny Näsholm. The group investigates plant nitrogen nutrition, with a particular focus on the acquisition and utilization of organic nitrogen and their roles in plant physiology and growth. The project will be supervised day to day by Dr Ioanna Antoniadi-Nilsson.
The Postdoc. will be employed at The Department of Forest Ecology and Management. The department includes about 120 people of which 9 are professors. Our mission is to advance the understanding of forest ecosystems and how these should be managed today and in the future.
For more information: http://www.slu.se/en/departments/forest-ecology-management/
Read more about our benefits and working at SLU by visiting: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/
Umeå is a leading centre for plant science, with a highly collaborative, international research environment and modern facilities for plant growth, imaging and analytics. The candidate will have opportunities to develop an independent scientific profile, gain supervision experience and build an international network.
Location:
Umeå
Form of employment:
Temporary employment 36 months
Scope:
100%
Start date:
January 1 2027 or by agreement
Application:
Please submit your application before deadline 26 November  2026. You can submit your application by clicking the button below. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.
The application should be written in English and include:
A cover letter (max. 1 page) describing your motivation, research interests and how your experience fits the project
A CV, including a publication list
Copies of relevant degree certificates
Contact details of two or three referees 

Union representatives:
https://internt.slu.se/en/my-employment/employee-associations/kontaktpersoner-vid-rekrytering/
 
 
The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses. We strive to provide a work environment characterised by inclusivity and gender equality, where different experiences generate conversations between people and pave the way for science, creativity and development. Therefore, we welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

jobs.occupation: Doctoral student in Mechanical Engineering - specialisation in wire drawing
jobs.description:
Örebro University and the School of Science and Technology are looking for a doctoral student for the doctoral programme in Mechanical Engineering, concluding with a doctoral degree.
Start date: January – March 2027.
Project description
Steel wire is an essential component of countless products and applications, from everyday items such as ballpoint pens and car tyres to critical infrastructure such as buildings and bridges. As industry advances towards more sustainable manufacturing, there is an increasing need to produce steel wire products with greater resource efficiency, improved material performance, and reduced environmental impact.
This doctoral project aims to advance the knowledge and technologies needed to make wire drawing processes more efficient, robust, and sustainable. The research is carried out in close collaboration with the wire drawing industry, ensuring that scientific developments address real industrial challenges and contribute to more sustainable production of steel wire products. Particular emphasis will be placed on improving process understanding and developing and evaluating innovative drawing tools.
The research will combine experimental investigations of wire drawing processes, tool behaviour, and resulting wire properties with sensor-based measurements, data analysis, and modelling. A central objective is to understand how material properties, process conditions, lubrication, and tooling interact and influence process performance, tool wear, and wire quality. This knowledge will support the development of practical solutions that improve resource utilisation, extend tool life, and enhance the efficiency and sustainability of industrial wire drawing.
As a doctoral student, you will plan and conduct experiments, analyse data, develop models, and communicate your findings through scientific publications and presentations. You will work closely with academic researchers and industrial partners, contributing to research that bridges fundamental scientific understanding and practical industrial applications.
The project offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the intersection of mechanical engineering, manufacturing technology, materials engineering, measurement technology, modelling, and control engineering. By addressing challenges associated with resource efficiency, production performance, and the green transition, the research aims to contribute to the development of next-generation wire drawing processes and tools that support more sustainable steel wire production.
Supervision: The doctoral student will be supervised by Christer Korin (principal supervisor) and Joakim Larsson (assistant supervisor).
The programme and the doctoral studentship
The doctoral programme consists of courses and an independent research project that you will present in a doctoral thesis. The programme concludes with a doctoral degree and comprises 240 credits, which corresponds to four years of full-time study.
Our ambition is for your doctoral studies to be stimulating and purposeful throughout the programme until you have obtained your doctoral degree. A thorough introduction will therefore get you off to a good start and provide a solid foundation on which you can build your studies. As a doctoral student at Örebro University, you will be offered a specially tailored seminar series, covering matters ranging from doctoral programme rules and careers to support during the study period and networking.
The place on the programme is linked to a full-time doctoral studentship for the duration of the study programme, which corresponds to four years of full-time study. More information on doctoral studentships, part-time studies and part-time doctoral studentships can be found on https://www.oru.se/english/study/doctoral-studies/how-to-become-a-doctoral-student/. The initial salary for a doctoral studentship is SEK 32 300 a month (salary period 2025-2026).
Entry requirements and selection
To see the job advertisement in its entirety, visit: https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/job/?jid=20260303
Information
For more information about the programme and the doctoral studentship, contact Joakim Larsson, Associate Senior Lecturer, joakim.larsson@oru.se, +4619303378 or Christer Korin, Senior Lecturer, christer.korin@oru.se, +4619303082.
At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.
Application to the programme and for the doctoral studentship
The application is made online. Click the button “Apply” to begin the application procedure.
For the application to be complete, the following electronic documents must be included:
CV
Copies of the original certificate and official transcript for Bachelor's degree
Copies of the original certificate and official transcript for Master's degree
Independent project (degree project)
Other relevant documents, course and degree certificates verifying eligibility

As a main rule, application documents and attachments are to be written in Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, or English. Certificates and documents in other languages verifying your qualifications and experience must be translated by an authorised translator to Swedish or English. A list of authorised translators can be obtained from Kammarkollegiet (the Legal, Financial and Administrative Services Agency), http://www.kammarkollegiet.se/engelska/start.
When you apply for admission, you automatically also apply for a doctoral studentship.
More information for applicants will be found on our career site:  https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/
The application deadline is 2026-12-18. We look forward to receiving your application!
As we have already made our choices in terms of external collaboration partners and marketing efforts for this recruitment process, we decline any contact with recruitment agencies and advertisers.
As directed by the National Archives of Sweden (Riksarkivet), we are required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

Are you interested in the potential of citizens' assemblies and other democratic innovations to drive climate transformation? Come join us!
Work assignments 
The Environmental Change division (tema Miljöförändring) at the Department of Thematic Studies is looking to hire a two-year postdoctoral researcher specializing in democratic innovations.
You will be part of the Formas-funded research project Democratic Innovations for Climate Transformation (2027-2029), which entails a systematic and interdisciplinary knowledge synthesis of how climate citizens’ assemblies and related democratic processes can contribute to system transformation. The project explores what the existing research literature tells us about the political impact of climate assemblies, how they might contribute to broader systemic transformations, and what this means for Swedish climate governance.
As postdoc on the project, you will take a leading role in carrying out the systematic literature review across academic databases and grey literature, following established standards for searching, screening, and quality assessment. You will contribute centrally to the comparative synthesis of findings across studies, and to identifying evidence gaps in how deliberative processes connect to system-level transformation. You will also help design and facilitate stakeholder dialogues with Swedish municipalities and practitioners, which ensures that the resulting knowledge is robust and genuinely useful for policy and practice.
You will work in close collaboration with the project’s principal investigator and a research team from LiU and Stockholm Resilience Centre. There is considerable room to help shape the project’s methodological choices and analytical framework, and to co-author academic outputs arising from the review and synthesis work.
As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.
Qualifications
To be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.
Your doctoral degree should preferably have been awarded no more than three years ago. If there are special reasons, a degree awarded more than three years ago may be accepted. Special reasons include sick leave, parental leave, trade union positions of trust, service in the defense, or other similar circumstances, as well as service or assignments relevant to the subject area.
We are looking for someone with a doctoral degree in social sciences, humanities, or related fields, and a demonstrated familiarity with the research area of democratic innovations – for example, deliberative democracy, citizens’ assemblies, participatory governance, or environmental/climate governance. Experience carrying out systematic literature reviews and others forms of qualitative content analysis is considered a merit. So is prior experience with stakeholder involvement and co-production through workshops and similar formats.
You are curious, rigorous, and comfortable moving between the fine-grained work of systematic screening and coding and the bigger-picture task of synthesizing what it all means. You enjoy working collaboratively, taking initiative, and are able to communicate complex research to non-academic audiences, such as policymakers and practitioners. A strong command of written and spoken English is required.
The workplace
You will be employed at the Department of Thematic Studies where you will be affiliated with the Environmental Change theme. You can read about the workplace https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/tema/temam.
The employment
This employment is a temporary full-time contract of two years. Starting date is Januari 1, 2027, or as soon as possible. 
Salary and employment benefits
At Linköping University, salaries are set individually and differentiated, in accordance with the applicable collective agreements (RALS/RALS-T) and the university’s salary-setting guidelines.
More information about employee benefits is available https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/employee-benefits.
Union representatives
Information about union representatives, see https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/hjalp%20for%20sokande.
Application procedure
Apply for the position by clicking the “Apply” button. Your application must be received no later than 27 November, 2026.
Applications and documents received after the date above will not be considered. 
Please attach your selected research publications electronically, in pdf or word format, in the application template. Research publications, e.g. monographs, which cannot be sent electronically should be sent in three sets by mail to the University Registrar at Linköping University, University Registrar, S-581 83 Linköping, Sweden. The publications must be received by Linköping University no later than the deadline for application. 
Please note that printed publications will not be returned. They will be archived at Linköping University. 
In the event of a discrepancy between the English translation of the job announcement and the Swedish original, the Swedish version shall take precedent. 
We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives - diversity enriches our work and helps us grow. Preserving everybody's equal value, rights and opportunities is a natural part of who we are. Read more about our work with: https://liu.se/en/article/lika-villkor/.
We look forward to receiving your application!
 
Linköping university has framework agreements and wishes to decline direct contacts from staffing- and recruitment companies as well as vendors of job advertisements.

jobs.description:
Merch that moves business needs a platform that moves just as fast.
From scattered purchases without brand control, to the magic that happens when it all clicks: merch that makes a real impact, on one global platform customized for each client, as if they built it themselves.
That’s what we’re building at Exakt. The platform is up and running, but this is only the beginning. Now comes the most advanced part, and we’re looking for an engineer with the drive and the skills to build it on a global scale. 
What you’ll do  You’ll build and own our merch platform, full stack: TypeScript and React on the frontend, Node APIs in the middle and a MedusaJS headless commerce backend, all running on GCP. 
It’s live with our first clients, and the codebase is still young enough that your decisions will stick. From here, you’ll:

Own the platform end to end, from architecture to checkout

Refine and develop the product logic. One t-shirt can come in 62 colors and seven sizes, from several suppliers, production partners and locations. Find new ways to make it all run even more smoothly

Take our client dashboard further, with the advanced features our clients didn’t know they needed, and even more transparency around orders, statistics and the environmental impact of what they buy

Automate the manual work, on the platform and behind the scenes, so the team can spend more time on the creative work

Set the technical direction with our founder, and help shape the team as we grow 

Who you are
You enjoy figuring out what’s needed and making it happen without waiting to be asked. And you’re curious about the business behind the code, whether you’re shaping a feature or talking ideas through with a client, in English.

You’re resourceful, and happy to use a smart existing solution instead of reinventing it

You bring experience and an open mind. You know how to move fast, and you’re always curious about new ways of working

You know when speed matters more than perfection, and you make sure the quick fix doesn’t become permanent

You work AI-first, and take security and client data just as seriously

You like people, and you’d rather be at the office with the team than on mute

You’re comfortable across backend and frontend, and our designers take care of the design. Experience with e-commerce, Medusa or multi-tenant platforms is a plus, but not a must. 
Tech you’ll work with  We’re guessing you already have the essentials. The limited editions are a bonus, and the rest you’ll pick up along the way.

The essentials: TypeScript, React, Node, PostgreSQL, Git, and GCP or a similar cloud platform

The limited editions: MedusaJS, Next.js, Redis, Prisma, Terraform, Clerk, Stripe 

About Exakt
Exakt, the world’s boldest merch agency since 2004. Bold, but true. We start with who a brand wants to reach and what it wants to say, and help turn that into products people keep, use and remember. Our clients feel safe with us. They know they’ll get the right thing, on time and delivered to the right place.
We’ve run webshops for our clients for more than 10 years. Now we’re scaling up our platform, continuously building new processes around our clients’ needs and our own workflow efficiency, and automating more and more of what has been done by hand. The whole process, and the service and ownership we’re known for, become transparent and easy to follow.
With new print techniques, new ways of working with our print partners and years of industry know-how, we have turned our knowledge into a platform that’s unique in our industry.
Picture a company where everyone, from sales and marketing to HR and finance, gets the merch they need from one place. Always on brand and always the strongest choice for the target group, whether it’s printed on demand, custom-made or shipped from stock, with full control over costs and climate impact. Behind it sits a multi-tenant platform built around each client. There’s no off-the-shelf solution for this, so we’re building our own.
We work with brands like Samsung, Electrolux and KRY, and things are going well: we’re profitable, growing fast and have never needed venture capital. Put our merch expertise together with a platform that handles every part of it, and you get something no one else offers.
Why Exakt
You’ll have real ownership of the tech from day one, with the influence of a startup in a company that’s already on solid ground. Exakt is known in our industry for always being a step ahead, in how we work with ideas, proposals, solutions and suppliers, so you really get the best of both worlds. We’re a team of eight with zero prestige, and we’re growing, looking for the right expertise to expand our team in every area. We support each other through whatever comes our way, celebrate together, eat lunch together and take our merch-cap throwing competitions a little too seriously.
You’ll find us at our office on Lidingö, where client work happens in English and office chat in Swedish, so you’ll need to understand it.
Apply
Sound like you? We’d love to hear from you. We review applications on a rolling basis, so there’s no need to wait.
Curious about something first? Emelie is helping us find the right person and is happy to answer anything about the role: emelie.stjarnas@ants.se

About the Role
We are looking for an IT Operations Engineer to join our Nordic IT Operations team and support our Swedish sites, serving approximately 640 employees across offices and manufacturing facilities.
In this role, you will provide first and second line IT support, helping to ensure stable, secure and efficient IT services across the business. You will support end users, maintain IT equipment, contribute to infrastructure improvements, and participate in both local and Nordic IT projects.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone early in their IT career who enjoys solving technical challenges, working closely with users, and developing their skills in a modern and international IT environment.

Principal Responsibilities and Accountabilities
End User Support

About You
We are looking for someone who enjoys helping others and is passionate about technology. You are organised, service-minded and eager to learn. You communicate effectively with colleagues at all levels and enjoy working collaboratively to solve problems.
You have gained at least 1-2 years of experience in IT support, service desk, or a similar technical role, with exposure to Microsoft 365, ticket management systems, and Active Directory. In addition, you take ownership of your work, have a structured approach to troubleshooting and are motivated by delivering reliable and efficient IT support in a fast-paced environment.
Whether you have recently started your IT career or already gained some experience in a support role, you are keen to continue growing your technical expertise while contributing to the success of the business.
You hold a degree, diploma, or equivalent qualification in Information Technology.
Desired Skills & Qualifications
Knowledge of Windows operating systems.
Knowledge of Microsoft 365 applications and services.
Experience installing and configuring IT hardware.
Basic understanding of networking concepts.
Familiarity with troubleshooting methodologies.
Understanding of incident and request management processes.
Experience with ticketing systems.
Basic awareness of ITIL principles.

Experience with Windows Server enviroments, SAP or ERP systems, and VPN/remote access tool knowledge is a plus! Nevertheless, we value curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn.

Why DS Smith?
At DS Smith, you'll be part of an international organisation where innovation, sustainability, and customer focus drive everything we do. We are passionate about developing smarter, more sustainable packaging solutions and empowering our people to make a real impact. Here, you'll have the opportunity to grow professionally and work alongside talented colleagues in a collaborative and supportive environment.
DS Smith is a leading packaging company operating in 34 countries with approximately 30,000 employees worldwide. To learn more about us, visit: www.dssmith.com
We want our employees to thrive both professionally and personally. That's why we offer a range of benefits that support health, wellbeing, and work-life balance, including private health insurance, dental care, regular health check-ups, subsidised lunch, among other benefits.

A Workplace for Everyone
At DS Smith, we believe that the best teams are built by people with diverse experiences, perspectives, and strengths. So, if this role feels right for you, but you do not meet every qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Your ambition, commitment, and potential can be just as important as meeting every requirement listed in the job advertisement.

Application and Further Information
The position is a permanent, full-time role and reports to the IT Operations Team Leader. A 6-month probationary period applies.
The starting date will be agreed upon individually; however, our ambition is to have the position filled as soon as possible.
Working hours: Monday to Friday, 07:45 to 16:30 (local time)
If you have further questions about the role, please contact Justin Hoveland, I&T Infrastructure Manager, at Justin.Hoveland@dssmith.com
For additional information or questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our recruitment team at nordic.recruitment@dssmith.com. Please note that we do not accept applications via email.
As part of our recruitment process, we use screening questions as well as logical reasoning and personality assessments to support a fair and objective selection process.
Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so don't wait to submit yours!
Please submit your application and CV in English.
We look forward to hearing from you soon!

Are you eager to build an international career across our end-to-end Supply Chain, powering renowned dairy brands such as Lurpak, Arla and Castello? Do you want responsibility from day one and the chance to lead strategic projects that shape how we plan, produce and move sustainable dairy? As a Supply Chain Graduate, you will gain broad, hands-on experience across our end-to-end Supply Chain, build a strong international network and accelerate your development towards future leadership roles in Arla.
 
About the Supply Chain Graduate Programme
The 2-year Supply Chain Graduate Programme offers an end-to-end perspective of Supply Chain with four rotations of 6 months each. You will develop your project leadership skills while gaining hands-on experience in Logistics, Production, Planning and Engineering & Technology. You will work on strategic projects in areas such as sustainability and digitalization and get the full perspective of Arla’s Supply Chain – from farm to fridge. This opportunity lets you explore your leadership potential, accelerating your career towards a leading role in our Global Supply Chain function to help shape the future of sustainable dairy.
 
We are looking for graduates to join the programme at one of our production sites in Denmark, Sweden, United Kingdom, and Germany. You will spend 18 months at your primary location and have a 6-month rotation abroad during the programme. We will assign you to the local site where we see the best fit for your development opportunities.
 
As a graduate in Supply Chain, you will be exposed to production sites, distribution centers, and warehouses. You and your fellow Supply Chain graduates will work on strategically important projects at your respective sites, all focusing on the same overall topics - such as sustainability, digitalization and lean optimization, among much more. The rotations are structured as follows

Second rotation In your second rotation, you will stay in the same location and work in Planning.
Third rotation In this rotation, you will go abroad to a different country and work with a co-graduate in Engineering & Technology.

How you will make an impact as a Supply Chain Graduate

Real responsibilities from day one enabling on-the-job learning
Leadership development camps, taking place in different markets with your graduate colleagues
One-to-one mentoring from senior leaders
An impactful graduate experience and access to a global graduate network

 
Across your four rotations you will
Lead and deliver projects that improve safety, quality, service, costs and sustainability
Work with data, digitalization and automation to optimize processes
Gain an understanding of the full Supply Chain
Build stakeholder management and change leadership skills in diverse, international teams

 
Are you our next Supply Chain graduate?   
To apply for the Supply Chain Graduate Programme, please ensure that you can tick off the following boxes
You are completing or have completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree between September 2025 and September 2027, preferably within supply chain, engineering, food/dairy science, operations, logistics, production or a related field
You have a strong interest in end-to-end supply chain, processes and operations with general business acumen and commercial interest being an advantage
Preferably minimum one year of relevant work experience from student jobs or minimum 6 months of internship
You are globally mobile and willing to go abroad for 6 months during the 2-year programme
International experience and cross-cultural understanding gained from working, studying or volunteering abroad will be considered a plus
You are fluent in English. Furthermore, it is an advantage if you speak Danish, German or Swedish

 
Additionally, we are looking for personal qualifications including
Clear leadership aspirations and the drive to deliver results
A global, curious mindset with strong relationship-building and influencing skills

Important information before application
The application period for the Supply Chain Graduate Programme runs from November 2nd 2026 to January 3rd 2027. Before applying, please make sure that you have already prepared your CV and cover letter in English. You will be asked different questions on the application page, thus we recommend that you start the application process from a computer instead of a mobile phone.
 
For additional information, read more about the Supply Chain Graduate Programme on our website. Here, you can get inspiration from some of our previous and current graduates and learn more about the programme. You can also read more about what to expect from the recruitment process.
 
Shape the Future of Dairy 
Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

jobs.occupation: PhD position in biology, specialisation in aquatic ecology
jobs.description:
Department of Aquatic Resources (SLU Aqua)
Third-cycle subject area
Biology
Description of the doctoral project
A PhD position in biology with specialisation in aquatic ecology is available at the Department of Aquatic Resources at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU Aqua). The theme of the PhD project is on management and conservation methods of critically endangered fishes, focusing on Anguillid eels. Trap and Transport (T&T) is a management method used to enable fish to continue their migration in fragmented riverine systems, and to reduce hydropower turbine mortality for downstream migrating fish. Today, we lack knowledge regarding how T&T should be conducted to optimize the method from an eel’s perspective. The aim of this project is to answer some of these knowledge gaps through field studies, experiments, analysis of existing data, modelling, and via international expert knowledge exchange. The main questions that will be addressed are:
 
How can the core aspects of the T&T process be optimized from an eel’s perspective?
How is T&T currently conducted in different countries and what can we learn from each other?
In which Swedish watersheds should T&T be prioritized today and in the future?
In addition, the project aims to develop best practice guidelines for T&T to be used at a national and international scale.

 
About the position
The main task is to conduct the PhD thesis work under supervision, including development of the PhD student's methodological, theoretical, analytical, writing, and presentation skills. The PhD student will conduct experiments in the field, including handling of eels, tagging and more. The work will be done at SLU Aqua in Drottningholm (Stockholm), and at various field sites.
 
The position includes collaboration with international researchers, and one of the co-supervisors is Dr. Derek Evans at the Agri-Food and Bioscience Institute (AFBI), Northern Ireland. The student will also collaborate closely with Dr. Jani Helminen, Natural Resources Institute (LUKE) Finland.
 
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
 
Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in biology. To meet the specific entry requirements, you must have at least 90 HEC in biology-related subjects. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 HEC must be at second-cycle level.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
 
Desirable experience
Experience with animal experiments and/or fieldwork.
Experience working with fish.
Experience with relevant practical and statistical methods.
Experience with independent writing.
Experience with organising workshops or large meetings.
Experience with analysis of large datasets.
Experience in collaboration with commercial fishers, industries and management agencies.
Will contribute to a good working climate.
Good communication skills in English, written and spoken.
Driver’s licence.
Great emphasis on personal qualities, collaboration skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and capacity for independent work.

 
About us
At the Department of Aquatic Resources (SLU Aqua) we are passionate about conservation and sustainable management of aquatic animals, including fish. We are geographically distributed across Sweden, and this PhD position will be based in Stockholm at the Institute of Freshwater Research, beautifully situated on the countryside on the island of Lovön right by lake Mälaren. We offer:
 
An excellent and professionally stimulating working environment with dedicated colleagues
Access to a broad international network of scientists
Salary as PhD research fellow in the state salary scale
Good welfare benefits

 
Read more about SLU Aqua: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/organisation/departments/aquatic-resources/
 
Read more about staff benefits and life as an SLU employee: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/
 
Read more about PhD courses and PhD study programmes: https://www.slu.se/en/study/programmes-courses/doctoral-education/ 
 
Form of employment and salary Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme)
Doctoral student’s salaries are set following the local collective agreement. Salary progression is fixed.
 
Scope
100%
 
Location
Drottningholm, Stockholm
 
Start date
2027-04-01, or upon agreement.
 
Application and selection Please submit your application using the link below. The deadline is 30 November 2027. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.
 
Read more about the attachments that your application should include at https://www.slu.se/en/study/programmes-courses/doctoral-education/how-can-i-become-a-doctoral-student/application/
 
Selection among eligible applicants is based on the documents attached to the application, and is carried out with regard to the applicant’s ability to complete the programme within the allotted time.
 
Academic union representatives
https://internt.slu.se/en/my-employment/employee-associations/kontaktpersoner-vid-rekrytering/
 
Note: This is a shortened version of the advertisement adapted to the Swedish Public Employment Service’s (Platsbanken) system. Please see the full advertisement on SLU’s website: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/jobs-and-vacancies/
 
The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses.

RFSL is seeking an International Advocacy Advisor to support Ukrainian LGBTQI organisations and activists in advancing their advocacy priorities and influencing policy at national, regional and international levels. The role combines international advocacy, partnership development and capacity strengthening, with practical programme and administrative support that enables locally led movements to thrive.
About RFSL and our international work
RFSL (the Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, and Intersex Rights), founded in 1950, is one of the world’s oldest non-profit organisations working to advance LGBTQI rights.
RFSL’s international work supports LGBTQI movements in Eastern Europe, Asia and Africa through regranting, partnerships, knowledge exchange, organisational support and advocacy. We work closely with local partners to support locally led movements, strengthen their agency and influence, and contribute to enabling environments for LGBTQI rights at national, regional and global levels.
Your role with us
You will work closely with Ukrainian LGBTQI organisations and activists to strengthen their ability to lead and influence advocacy processes. Together with partners, you will identify priorities, develop strategies and messaging, map stakeholders, and find opportunities to engage decision-makers and relevant international platforms, including the EU, UN, OSCE and Council of Europe.
A central part of the role is helping partners access the knowledge, networks, resources and practical support they need to pursue their priorities. This includes organising capacity-strengthening activities, managing scholarships and providing hands-on programme and administrative support. You will also contribute to advocacy efforts in Sweden related to Ukraine and work with RFSL colleagues to align policy, advocacy and communications.
You will collaborate with the Head of Program, International Program Managers, other Advocacy Advisors and colleagues across RFSL’s international work. The position is based in Stockholm and involves international travel several times per year.
For full description of  key responsibilities and desirable qualifications, please see our job ad on RFSL’s careers page
Who are you?
You are a structured, collaborative and solution-oriented professional committed to LGBTQI rights, international advocacy and locally led movement strengthening. You understand Ukraine’s political and social context, the regional human rights and civil society landscape, and the challenges facing LGBTQI organisations working in politically sensitive or resource-constrained environments.
You build trusted partnerships and adapt your approach to different organisations, particularly grassroots groups that may need substantial practical support alongside strategic guidance. You respect local leadership and autonomy, understand power dynamics in international partnerships, and approach your work with awareness of security, safeguarding and the importance of accountable support.
You enjoy combining strategic advocacy and capacity strengthening with practical operational and administrative tasks. You are comfortable moving between developing advocacy strategies and organising activities, coordinating travel, booking accommodation, handling receipts and ensuring that payments and documentation are in order. You recognise that this hands-on support is an important part of enabling partners to advance their own priorities.
You bring strong analytical, communication and organisational skills, can represent RFSL professionally with civil society, public authorities and international institutions, and work effectively across teams and cultures. You are proactive, flexible and accountable, and share RFSL’s values of anti-racism, feminism, accessibility and intersectionality.
To succeed in this role, you need:
A strong commitment to LGBTQI rights and experience or demonstrated competence in advocacy, policy influence, civil society support or related human rights work, particularly in relation to Ukraine.
Strong knowledge of the human rights situation and civil society landscape in Ukraine or the wider region, including experience working in partnership with LGBTQI movements or organisations.
At least three years of relevant professional experience in advocacy, civil society support, development cooperation or a related field.
Experience engaging with international or regional advocacy processes and human rights mechanisms, such as those of the EU, UN, OSCE or Council of Europe.
An understanding of security and safeguarding considerations when working with LGBTQI activists and civil society in challenging contexts.
Strong analytical, organisational and administrative skills, including experience with organisational capacity assessment, budgets, programme documentation and risk management.
Excellent written and spoken English.
Some understanding of Ukrainian or a closely related language, together with a willingness to develop Ukrainian-language skills as needed.
The ability to work from Stockholm, Sweden, and undertake international travel several times per year.

Employment terms
Employment type: This is a permanent position, starting with a six-month probationary period. 
Location: RFSL office in Stockholm.
Start date: As agreed
Contract terms: Covered by the Collective Agreement for Nonprofit Organizations

Our offer
RFSL offers an inclusive, values-driven workplace where you can contribute to meaningful change alongside committed colleagues and partners. We provide competitive employment conditions, including occupational pension and parental benefits.
How to apply
Apply by November 15th, 2026. The recruitment process is conducted in English and includes anonymous, competency-based assessment, a work-related assignment and a background check.
For questions about the position or recruitment process, contact HR Partner Tobias Jensen at tobias.jensen@rfsl.se.
RFSL strives to be an inclusive, feminist and anti-racist workplace. We welcome applicants regardless of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, sex characteristics, religion, race, ethnicity, country of origin, disability, age or other grounds of discrimination. We strongly encourage candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Öppen för alla
Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

Job Description
You understand paid media and love getting deep into data. If you have solid media knowledge and analytical depth, you are the one we are looking for.  

WHAT YOU WILL DO 
As Paid Media Analyst at H&M, you’ll build our understanding of how our media investment drives results across 60+ markets and 10+ channels, at a scale few companies can match. You’ll work with in-platform data, incrementality-based attribution and marketing mix modelling side by side, comparing what each one tells us and turning it into answers the business can act on. 
This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend most of your time in the data, not in strategy meetings, but your analysis will directly shape how we invest. You’ll own your analyses from start to finish and help build how we measure and report paid media at H&M. 
 
Your responsibilities will include: 
Analyse: Dig into paid media and business performance data to understand what’s driving results, find root causes behind changes in performance, and spot opportunities for testing and optimisation. 
Connect: Bring these measurement sources together across channels and markets into one consistent view of performance. 
Advise: Turn analysis into clear recommendations and compelling narratives for media and marketing teams, and contribute to insights shared with leadership all the way up.  
Build: Shape reporting frameworks, dashboards and automated reporting together with BI and data specialists. 

 
WHO YOU ARE 
 
The two things we can’t compromise on are strong hands-on analytical skills and a solid understanding of paid media. You don’t need to be an expert in every platform, but you should understand the media landscape, its key metrics and how to use data to find what’s driving performance. 
 
You bring: 
3+ years of experience in marketing analytics or a similar role, working with large datasets to analyse media and marketing performance. 
Experience working with large data sets, from channels such as Meta, Google or TikTok. You don’t need to have run campaigns yourself, but you know what the data means. 
Familiarity with measurement beyond platform reporting, such as attribution modelling, incrementality measurement, or marketing mix modelling. 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through open questions independently. 
Experience owning analyses end-to-end and turning them into clear, actionable recommendations, supported by strong visualization and storytelling. 
Experience working cross-functionally with different stakeholder groups. Experience presenting to senior stakeholders is a plus. 
Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills. 
Fluency in English. 

You’re curious, structured and comfortable with ambiguity. You’d rather dig into why the numbers moved than write the strategy, but you understand how your work feeds into it. Most of all, you’re excited to use data to influence real business decisions. 
 
WHY JOIN US? 
Media is one of the main ways H&M reaches and engages customers around the world. You’ll join a team with strong media expertise around you. Your role is to bring the analytical perspective, challenge what the data is telling us, and help turn complexity into clear decisions. 

WHO WE ARE 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. 
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, scale and knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. 

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE 
At H&M Group, you’ll be part of an international and collaborative environment where your ideas and perspectives matter. Alongside opportunities to learn, develop and build your career across H&M Group, we offer a range of benefits. 
Your H&M Group benefits include: 
Employee discount: As an H&M Group employee, you receive an employee discount across eligible H&M Group brands, in stores and online where applicable. Brands include H&M, H&M HOME, H&M Move, COS, Monki, Weekday, & Other Stories and ARKET. 
H&M Incentive Program (HIP).
Wellbeing allowance: Employees in Sweden receive an annual wellbeing allowance, supporting activities that contribute to health and wellbeing. 
Holiday in advance: You have the option to take holiday in advance during your first year of employment. 

Moving to Stockholm? 
If you’re currently based outside Sweden, we know that taking on a new role can also mean taking a big step personally. We’ll support you through the relocation process, from preparing for your move to getting established in Sweden and finding accommodation. Our aim is to make the transition as smooth as possible so that you can focus on your new role and life in Stockholm. 

JOIN US 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things: our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values and opportunities for growth. Most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are. 
This is a full-time permanent position based in Stockholm, Sweden. The desired start date for the role is as soon as possible. 
Apply by submitting your CV in English as soon as possible. Due to data policies, we only accept applications through our career page. 
We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter to your application.

Department of Biosystems and Technology
PhD Project: Valorization and Risk Assessment of Anaerobic Digestates for Sustainable Horticultural Production
Third-cycle subject area: Horticultural Science
Description of the doctoral project
 
The transition to circular food and energy systems requires safe, high-quality products that can return nutrients and organic matter to horticultural production. Anaerobic digestate from biogas production is a promising resource containing plant nutrients and organic fibre originating from, for example, manure, food and household waste, slaughterhouse by-products, park and garden residues, and biomass from intermediate crops or roadside vegetation. The digestate can be separated into a nutrient-rich liquid fraction and a fibre fraction. While the liquid fraction has potential for use in nutrient solutions, the fibre fraction is particularly relevant as a constituent of growing media and a potential partial replacement for peat and other fibre materials. Developing safe, functional and locally available alternatives to peat is an important challenge for sustainable horticultural production. A key barrier is the possible presence of pyralid herbicide residues. These herbicides can accumulate in crop material, persist during anaerobic digestion and cause growth disturbances in sensitive horticultural crops at very low concentrations. The project will investigate the occurrence and fate of pyralids in selected feedstocks and digestate fractions, with particular focus on the fibre fraction and its use in growing media.
About the position
The doctoral project will combine greenhouse and growth-chamber bioassays with laboratory studies and chemical characterisation. It will assess effects on plant growth and nutrient uptake, examine the distribution, degradation and immobilisation of herbicide residues, and generate knowledge to support risk assessment and the safe valorisation of digestate-derived growing-media products. The project is an important part in the ongoing transition for more circular productions systems where plant nutrients and fiber is recycled from waste to production. The project is a part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center, which means that there will be collaboration with other PhD students both at SLU and at Linköping University. Communication of results, both orally and in writing to both academic and industrial stakeholders are also important parts of the project. As a PhD-student, you will also take PhD courses and be a part of the daily work at the department.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Horticultural Science. To meet the specific entry requirements the applicant must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
You should have received a degree at advanced level (second cycle) within the fields of Horticultural Science, Agricultural Science, or similar subject. 
You should also have documented experience with laboratory work and experimental work within the field of study.
Beneficial competences 
Driver’s licence valid in Sweden. 
Documented experience from scientific writing and scientific communication.
Your profile
We are looking for an engaged and self-going candidate with genuine interest in horticulture and circular solutions. Suitable backgrounds are as a Horticulturist or Agronomist. Experience with laboratory work, for example microbial analyses, is beneficial. You should also have experience with practical plant cultivation. Great emphasis will be put on personal skills like curiosity, ability to work individually and in group, and ability to independently plan and perform research related tasks. You are expected to be open to new challenges and to take on various work tasks to contribute to the development of the department’s activities. Very good skills in speaking and writing in English is mandatory.
About us
At the department of Biosystems and Technology you will work in a multi-disciplinary environment together with around 60 colleagues, among which around 10 PhD students. The holder of this position will be a part of a national, transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities (Linköping University and SLU) and about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system and has additional support from Swedish Energy Agency. 
All doctoral positions advertised within BSRC will be formulated so that they fit into the competence center's research plans and at the same time reflect our parties' interests. This way, we ensure long-term competence supply to both industry and academia.
Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/
Form of employment / Funding
 
Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme).
 
Location:
 
Alnarp, Sweden

100%

Upon agreement, but preferably 2027-01-01.

Please submit your application using the link below. The deadline is November 27, 2026. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.
Read more about the attachments that your application should include at https://www.slu.se/en/study/programmes-courses/doctoral-education/how-can-i-become-a-doctoral-student/application/
Selection among eligible applicants is based on the documents attached to the application, and is carried out with regard to the applicant’s ability to complete the programme within the allotted time.
